result.title: TailDART: Compute-Efficient Foundation Models for Financial Time-Series Forecasting
result.summary: Although time-series foundation models (TSFMs) achieve strong zero-shot transferability across high-information-density physical systems, applying overparameterized TSFMs to quantitative finance is fundamentally constrained by low signal-to-noise ratios, non-stationarity, and prohibitive autoregressive decoding latency. To reconcile representation learning with institutional operational constraints, this study presents TailDART, a dense 2.68 million-parameter foundation model engineered for financial time-series forecasting. By integrating grouped-query attention into a lightweight backbone, the architecture drastically reduces Key-Value cache memory bandwidth overhead, achieving major inference acceleration (up to 48.1%) over prevailing state-of-the-art TSFMs to enable low-latency, high-throughput streaming execution. Furthermore, multi-asset benchmarks across varying temporal resolutions show that a compact model can remain competitive for market forecasting: TailDART matches the predictive fidelity of substantially larger baselines while demonstrating superior error resilience in high-volatility regimes.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出面向金融时间序列预测的轻量基础模型 TailDART，通过分组查询注意力降低 KV cache 带宽开销以加速推理，并在多资产基准上验证其预测精度与高波动鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作聚焦金融时序预测与推理加速，不涉及视觉或多模态推理中的 latent 状态生成、证据使用或停止决策；KV cache 效率虽与缓存结构有关，但无针对 latent 表示或推理动态的分析线索，故排除。
